target_customer: Software companies and enterprises that need fine grained authorization for applications, including AI access control
problem: Application permissions are hard to build and scale; AuthZed offers SpiceDB, an open source permissions database inspired by Google's Zanzibar, plus managed and enterprise versions.
business_model: Open source core with paid managed cloud, dedicated hosting and enterprise licenses

founders.name: Jake Moshenko
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 15 years building infrastructure tools; met Joey on the Google APIs team in 2010.

founders.name: Jimmy Zelinskie
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, software engineer and product leader focused on bringing hyperscaler authorization practices to the industry.

founders.name: Joseph Schorr
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder without bio and refers to Joey meeting Jake at Google; the identification as Joey is inferred by the page text.

technical_complexity.rationale: Implementing a Zanzibar style globally consistent permissions database with consistency tokens is distributed systems work.

defensibility.rationale: Once permissions data lives in the database it is hard to move, and the open source project builds community, but other open source Zanzibar implementations emerged.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later comparison pages list Ory Keto, OpenFGA and Oso as alternatives; the company stayed independent and raised a 2024 Series A.

market_need_then: Authorization was a recurring pain for the founders at CoreOS Quay, where customer permission demands outgrew simple role models, per the YC page, and Google's Zanzibar paper offered a design for it.

branding.name_origin: Authorization shortened, with the letter Z standing for authorization according to the brand guidelines; logo inspired by Arrakis from Dune

identity.logo: Letter Z mark and shifting sands motif from Arrakis
identity.mascot_or_character: Dibs, the SpiceDB mascot introduced in March 2025
identity.visual_style: Dune themed developer brand with a guidelines site

branding.brand_signature: SpiceDB and the Dune reference with the Dibs mascot
branding.community_and_virality: Open source SpiceDB with images on Docker Hub, Quay and GitHub, a DEV community presence and Cloudcast podcast appearance.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong themed developer brand for SpiceDB with a mascot and guidelines, though AuthZed as a name is hard to spell and the brand is known mainly among infrastructure engineers.

outcome_analysis: AuthZed joined YC in Winter 2021 with founders who had built Quay at CoreOS and worked at Google, raised a 3.9 million dollar seed that year and a 12 million dollar Series A in June 2024 led by General Catalyst. The open source SpiceDB project and rising need for AI access control drive its position. Open source competitors remain the main pressure.
